compensating.why: hop 3 reports a change whenever the size differs
hop 2 removes the key whenever its values are empty
hop 1 also requires that the value is no longer among the values

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which element of the key's collection is removed: it scans the iterator for the first element equal to the value and removes it through the iterator. Hop 1 only looks up the key's collection (an unmapped key gives null) and maps the change flag to the value passed in or null; hop 2 only removes the key after a change that leaves the collection empty; hop 3 only derives the change flag from the collection's size before and after one traversal; hop 4 passes the iterator on. On the trigger input the key holds no element equal to the value, so the gold's documented contract (remove the first remaining element equal to the value) allows no removal, yet the variant removes the last element the scan returned; the collection is then really smaller, so every caller reports the change truthfully and none can restore the element. The convention is pinned outside the gold: CursorableLinkedList.remove(Object), list.AbstractLinkedList.remove(Object) and MultiHashMap.removeMapping remove only an equal element and change nothing otherwise; TestCursorableLinkedList::testRemove and TestMultiHashMap::testRemove_KeyItem pin the absent case on those siblings, and TestMultiValueMap::testTotalSize, testSize_Key and testMapEquals pass through the chain (exactly the present value removed, the emptied key removed).
